overall: The AG found the Working Group a subcommittee that violated the OML by not posting notice or keeping minutes; the March 4 notice and March 13 roll-call allegations were rejected, and other allegations were declined.

allegations.summary: Notice of the March 4 meeting topic (Burnett Field lighting within 100 ft of a wetland) allegedly misidentified the field address and lacked lighting detail.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, the notice was sufficiently specific as to the reference to lighting.

allegations.summary: Whether the three-member Working Group formed by the Permanent Building Committee is a subcommittee subject to the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: In light of the Working Group’s ongoing role, carrying out work of the Committee and making recommendations to the Committee, we find that the Working Group is a subcommittee of the Committee.

allegations.summary: The Working Group allegedly met and communicated without posting notice or creating minutes of its meetings.
allegations.key_passage: Furthermore, we find that where the Working Group failed to create and approve minutes for its meetings, it violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: The Committee allegedly delegated creation of meeting notices and minutes to an outside contractor.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not dictate who must create notices or minutes; nor must minutes reflect the date of receipt or posting.

allegations.summary: Posted minutes allegedly do not show when they were received and posted online.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not dictate who must create notices or minutes; nor must minutes reflect the date of receipt or posting.

allegations.summary: Meeting notices allegedly are generic and boilerplate, with no specific notice identified as insufficient.
allegations.key_passage: Our office will not conduct broad audits of public bodies based on generalized allegations.

allegations.summary: The Committee chair allegedly cut short the complainant's public comment at the March 13 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Because the allegation that his public comment was cut short, even if true, would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law in any event, we decline to review this allegation.

allegations.summary: No roll call was allegedly taken at the start of the Committee's March 13 meeting to announce members.
allegations.key_passage: Where no Committee members participated in the meeting remotely, the Committee was not obligated to announce the names of members in attendance or vote by roll call.

allegations.summary: Minutes were allegedly not approved by roll call at the Committee's March 13 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Where no Committee members participated in the meeting remotely, the Committee was not obligated to announce the names of members in attendance or vote by roll call.

remedy: Within 60 days, the Working Group must create minutes for its meetings and certify to the AG's office that it has done so.

Within 60 days, the Working Group must publicly release emails among a quorum about matters within its jurisdiction, by reading them aloud at an open meeting or attaching them to open-meeting minutes.
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements.
remedy_passage: We order the Working Group, within 60 days of the date of this letter, to create minutes for its meetings and that it certify to our office that it has done so.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
